rationale: Experiment for the growth investigation that tests a claim recorded in its counterevidence: that the staged alternative (AddNonvoter first, AddVoter only when the server is ready) keeps a single-voter cluster serving while the named server is absent. The existing growth harness is extended with AddNonvoter variants of both the absent and the present cases, so the same observation phases now run for the voter and the non-voter form of the call. Native local feedback in a scratch copy inside draft showed the non-voter variants keeping the leader, but the retained execution decides.

experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and growth staging, extended with AddNonvoter variants of the absent and present cases so that the staged alternative recorded as counterevidence is executed rather than assumed; the case names carry the distinction (absent_server versus absent_server_nonvoter, control_present_server versus present_server_nonvoter).

scope.description: Four subtests on a one-voter cluster built by MakeCluster(1): absent_server and control_present_server call AddVoter for a second server that is either unwired and not running or running beforehand, and absent_server_nonvoter and present_server_nonvoter make the same calls through AddNonvoter. Each case records the configuration entry's commit status, samples the node's state, term, commit and last index every 25 ms for 1500 ms, makes a bounded client write, attempts two bounded repairs (RemoveServer and AddNonvoter for the named server), samples the node every 50 ms for a further three seconds, and then, in the absent cases, starts the named server and records whether the cluster recovers.
assumptions: AddNonvoter is the staged alternative the library still supports, because a non-voter receives log entries without counting for the configuration's quorum.
The two forms of the call differ only in the suffrage the named server receives; the rest of the staging is identical.
Bootstrap a single voter and grow it is the sequence BootstrapCluster's documentation recommends.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss.
excluded: No production code is modified and no fault is injected.
No offline recovery or restart is performed.

experiment.prefix: Each subtest prints growth_before, growth_window, growth_write_attempt, growth_api_repair_attempt and growth_recovery; the case is identified by mode (absent_server, control_present_server, absent_server_nonvoter, present_server_nonvoter).
